idiom_name: Foundation Decimal inside a Money struct with an ISO 4217 currency value
implementation_notes: Foundation ships Decimal, a base-10 value with about 38 significant digits whose rounding goes through NSDecimalRound and NSDecimalNumber.RoundingMode (.bankers, .plain, .down, .up), so the arithmetic primitive is a platform type; what is missing is the money value itself, hence a struct holding Decimal plus a currency identity with the rounding applied explicitly, because the framework's arithmetic functions take the mode per call rather than from a context. Codable conformance should encode the amount as a string or a minor-unit integer beside the currency code, since JSON has no decimal, and operators must reject mismatched currencies by construction. When ISO metadata, parsing and formatting should come from a package instead, SwiftCurrency supplies typed currencies with their minor units.
pitfalls: Decimal lives in Foundation, not the standard library, and its FloatingPoint conformance is incomplete (no infinity), so Double-based rates must be converted explicitly.
Decimal arithmetic truncates unless NSDecimalRound is called, and the rounding mode is a per-call argument rather than part of a context.
Encoding a Decimal as a JSON number converts through Double at some point in the pipeline, so the string form belongs in Codable.
